JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 21-09-2022 the petitioner was proceeding on a Yamaha A-2 motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KA-6660 as a pillion rider, the same was ridden by its rider-cum-RC owner by name Sharon towards Kaggalipura, on Bengaluru- Kanakapura road, in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations.

While so proceeding, at about 10.30 a.m., near Ravishankar Guruji Ashrama, Udipalya, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru, due to negligent riding of the rider of said motorcycle he lost control over said vehicle and applied sudden break.
Consequent the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Cura Hospital, Konanakunte, wherein she took first aid treatment and then she was shifted to NIMHANS Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, she was B.Com student and apart from that she was conducting tuitions and she was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
But, due to accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The Kaggalipura Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The the respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

He has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses Likitha C vs Sharon Colaso on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57186688/
2 and treatment taken by her.

Further he has contended that, he was riding his Yamaha A-2 motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KA-6660 on the extreme left side on Bengaluru-Kanakapura road, slowly and cautiously, by observing the traffic rules and regulations and while so proceeding at about 10.30 a.m., near Ravishankar Guruji Ashrama, Udipalya, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru, due to rough and big holes on the said road, without alternative he applied break and there was no negligence on his part.
Hence the claim petition against him is liable to be dismissed.
He has admitted that he is the R.C. owner of the Yamaha A-2 motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KA-6660.
The registration certificate and such other relevant documents pertaining to the said motorcycle are standing in his name.

The said vehicle was insured with the respondent No.2/Go Digit General Insurance Co. Ltd., vide policy No.D054807818/17012022, valid from 18-01-2022 to 17-01- 2023 and the said policy was in force as on the date of accident and he was also possessing valid and effective driving licence to ride the same.

sentences.text: Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it has prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Likewise, the respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy covering liability only for the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KA-6660 and risk of pillion rider is not covered under the policy and liability to indemnify the respondent No.1 is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 150 of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the risk of injured is not covered under this policy and there is no extra premium paid to cover the risk of pillion rider.
Hence, the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
It has contended that, the rider of the offending motorcycle was not holding valid and effective driving licence to ride the same as on the date of accident.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by her.
It has denied the occurrence of the accident and involvement of the motorcycle in the alleged accident.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it has prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 21-09-2022 at about 10.30 a.m., due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Yamaha A-2 Motorcycle bearing registration No.KA- 05-KA-6660 ?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?

7. In order to prove her case, the petitioner has got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked total 9 documents as Ex.P.1 to 9 and closed her side.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has got examined its representative/Associate Legal Claim as R.W.1 and got marked total 2 documents as Ex.R.1 and 2 and closed its side.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence on his behalf.
8. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material available on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 21-09-2022 when she was proceeding on a Yamaha A-2 motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KA-6660 as a pillion rider, towards Kaggalipura, on Bengaluru-Kanakapura road, near Ravishankar Guruji Ashrama, Udipalya, Uttarahalli Hobli,
Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of said motorcycle, he lost control over said vehicle and applied sudden break.
Consequent the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, she was B.Com student and apart from that she was conducting tuitions and she was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
But, due to accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
11. In order to prove her case, the petitioner has examined herself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein she has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of her oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 9 documents as Ex.P.1 to 9.

Out of the said documents, the Ex.P.1 is certified copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is certified copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is certified copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is certified copy of Motor Vehicles Accident report, Ex.P.5 is certified copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.6 is certified copy of charge- sheet, Ex.P.7 is notarized copy of Aadhar card, Ex.P.8 are medical bills (total 27) and Ex.P.9 are prescriptions (total 10).

12. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 6, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question is caused due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending Yamaha A-2 motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KA-6660 and applying sudden break.
Further it reveals that, due to said impact, the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries to head, hands and legs.

The investigation officer has clearly stated in his Ex.P.6 final report/charge-sheet that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KA-6660 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

4 13.

At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KA-6660 in the alleged accident, issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

The respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and the respondent No.1 has taken specific defence that, the said accident has taken place due to rough and big holes on the said road and there was no rash and negligent driving on his part.
But, the respondent No.1 & 2 have failed to establish the said contentions.
The respondent No.1 has neither adduced any evidence, nor produced any document to establish the said contentions.

Except the self serving statements of the R.W.1, who is the representative/Associate Legal Claim, there is no other oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the accident has taken place due to bad road condition and there was no rash and negligent driving on the part of the respondent No.1.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the respondent No.1/rider of offending motorcycle.
Though the learned counsel for respondents No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of her evidence.

14. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazer also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the extreme left side of 20 feet wide Bengaluru-Kanakapura road, near Ravishankar Guruji Ashrama, Udipalya, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru, due to sudden application of break by the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KA-6660.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.4, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KA-6660.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing has been brought out in the cross- examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has taken place due to bad condition of the road and there was no negligence on the part of the respondent No.1/rider of offending motorcycle.

The investigation officer has clearly stated in his final report that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KA-6660.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the owner or rider of said vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
15. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.5 wound certificate, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
She has suffered left temporal burst lobe with right FTP thin acute SDH and fracture of right temporal bone with diffuse cerebral edema.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondents No.1 and 2, to show that the above medical records are false documents.

There is absolutely no material on record Likitha C vs Sharon Colaso on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57186688/
5 to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KA-6660 and injuries sustained to the petitioner in the said accident 16.

Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
18.

sentences.text:
Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the reasons stated above, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that,
she has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 21-09-2022 at about 10.30 a.m., on Bengaluru-Kanakapura road, near Ravishankar Guruji Ashrama, Udipalya,
Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KA-6660.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

While answering the above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has caused due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KA-6660 and she has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.
The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e.
pecuniary

damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
The petitioner has deposed that, earlier to the accident, she was B.Com student and apart from that she was conducting tuitions and she was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her learning capacity.
But, the petitioner has neither produced any document nor examined any doctor to establish that, due to injuries sustained in the accident she has suffered any physical disability or deformity.

The petitioner has failed to prove that, due to accidental injuries she has suffered physical disability and she is not in a position to perform her regular work and thereby, she has lost her learning capacity.

In such circumstances, the Likitha C vs Sharon Colaso on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57186688/
6 question of awarding compensation under head loss of future income due to permanent physical disability does not arise at all.

entities.text: Likitha C vs Sharon Colaso on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
ii) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has deposed that, she has incurred expenses of Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, she has produced 27 medical bills, as per Ex.P.8.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.85,240/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.85,240/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:
In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e. left temporal burst lobe with right FTP thin acute SDH and fracture of right temporal bone with diffuse cerebral edema.
As per Ex.P.8 medical bills, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for one day on 21-09-2022, in Cura Hospitals, Bengaluru.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.8 medical bills, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for one day in Cura Hospitals, Bengaluru.
She might have spent some amount towards attendant charges during the said period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 1 = Rs.1,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.8 medical bills, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for one day in Cura Hospitals, Bengaluru.
She might have spent some amount towards food and nourishment during the said period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 1 = Rs.800/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Shastrinagar, BSK 2nd Stage, Bengaluru,
the accident has occurred on Bengaluru-Kanakapura road, near Ravishankar Guruji Ashrama,
Udipalya, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru and he has taken treatment at Cura Hospitals, Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between all the above three places, compensation of Rs.2,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before the accident she was B.Com student and apart from that she was conducting tuitions and she was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Further, she has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident she is unable to do her work.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove her avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.

She has not produced any document to show that, before accident she was B.Com student and she was Likitha C vs Sharon Colaso on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57186688/
7 conducting tuitions and she was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2022.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month.
The petitioner has taken treatment for one day as in-patient at Cura Hospitals, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries caused to her.
She might have taken rest for about two monthd and lost her income for the said period.
Therefore, Rs.15,500 x 2 = Rs.31,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 19 years and unfortunately she has suffered grievous injuries in the said accident and undergone treatment for one day as in-patient at Cura Hospitals,
Bengaluru.
Further, it might have took two month for complete curing of the injuries suffered by her.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities during the treatment period would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The petitioner has neither adduced any evidence nor produced any document to show that she requires any further treatment for the injuries sustained in the accident.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding future medical expenses does not arise at all.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.

20. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Nil 2.
Medical expenses 85,240-00 3. Pain and sufferings 40,000-00 4. Attendant charges 1,000-00 5.
Food and nourishment 800-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 2,000-00 7. Loss of income during 31,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 20,000-00
9. Future medical expenses -Nil-

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,80,040/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

8 21.
Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

As per Ex.R.2 insurance policy, the policy bearing No.D054807818/17012022 issued by the respondent No.2, in respect of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-05-KA-6660, was valid from 18-01-2022 to 17-01-2023.
But, it is pertinent to note that, the said policy is two-wheeler liability only policy and it does not covers the risk of pillion rider.
No additional premium has been collected by the respondent No.2 in respect of risk coverage of pillion rider.
It covers the risk of third-party liability only.

It is well settled principle of law that,
the pillion rider cannot be treated as a third party.
22.

The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.174/2018 (MV-D) C/w MFA No.6621/2018 (MV-D), in between The National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Sanaulla Khan and others, has clearly held that, "pillion rider is not covered when it is the 'Act only policy' (Liability only Policy) and no extra premium was collected for covering the risk of the pillion rider, the pillion rider or occupant of the car cannot come within the purview of the 'Third Party'.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Sanaulla Khan and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The insurance company is not liable to pay compensation, the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation."

23. As the Ex.R.2 insurance policy does not cover the risk of occupant/pillion rider, as on the date of accident, this Court is of the opinion that, the respondent No.2 insurance company is not liable to indemnify the insured/respondent No.1.

Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, as on the date of accident the risk of occupant/pillion rider was not covered by the Ex.R.2 insurance policy, issued in respect of offending motorcycle bearing bearing Reg. No. KA-05-KA-6660, the respondent No.2 insurance company is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Accordingly, holding that the respondent No.1 being the owner of offending vehicle is liable to pay the above compensation amount Rs.1,80,040/- to the petitioner, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,80,040/- (Rupees one lakh eighty thousand and forty only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner and he is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
The petition against respondent No.2 is dismissed.

The respondent No.1 has neither adduced any evidence, nor produced any document to establish the said contentions.
Except the self serving statements of the R.W.1, who is the representative/Associate Legal Claim, there is no other oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the accident has taken place due to bad road condition and there was no rash and negligent driving on the part of the respondent No.1.
When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KA-6660.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing has been brought out in the cross- examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has taken place due to bad condition of the road and there was no negligence on the part of the respondent No.1/rider of offending motorcycle.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
15. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.5 wound certificate, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
She has suffered left temporal burst lobe with right FTP thin acute SDH and fracture of right temporal bone with diffuse cerebral edema.
In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KA-6660 and injuries sustained to the petitioner in the said accident 16.
Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,80,040/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Likitha C vs Sharon Colaso on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57186688/
8 21.
Admittedly, as on the date of accident the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
But, it is pertinent to note that, the said policy is two-wheeler liability only policy and it does not covers the risk of pillion rider.
No additional premium has been collected by the respondent No.2 in respect of risk coverage of pillion rider.
It covers the risk of third-party liability only.
It is well settled principle of law that,
the pillion rider cannot be treated as a third party.
22.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.174/2018 (MV-D) C/w MFA No.6621/2018 (MV-D), in between The National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Sanaulla Khan and others, has clearly held that, "pillion rider is not covered when it is the 'Act only policy' (Liability only Policy) and no extra premium was collected for covering the risk of the pillion rider, the pillion rider or occupant of the car cannot come within the purview of the 'Third Party'.
The insurance company is not liable to pay compensation, the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation."
23. As the Ex.R.2 insurance policy does not cover the risk of occupant/pillion rider, as on the date of accident, this Court is of the opinion that, the respondent No.2 insurance company is not liable to indemnify the insured/respondent No.1.
